response.consequence: A client with administrator access can make the audit log endpoint return a 500 error by sending optimized_pagination=true with a negative-offset cursor. The new "advanced" mode has no working behavior for the negative-offset case it was written for.
response.explanation: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0, the code runs queryset[cursor.offset:stop] with a negative start. The code comment says Django handles this, but Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing or slicing and raise AssertionError("Negative indexing is not supported."). The audit log endpoint sets enable_advanced_features=True for superusers and global-access members who pass optimized_pagination=true. A cursor string with a negative offset, such as "0:-1:1", therefore crashes the request instead of paginating. The same branch computes stop = start_offset + limit + extra, so for a negative start the stop can also be negative. Even if the slice were accepted, it would not return the "data beyond normal pagination bounds" the comment describes. The related BasePaginator change leaves negative offsets unclamped when cursor.is_prev is true, so the base paginator keeps the same failure for prev cursors, and the new comment there ("safe because the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions") is wrong. I did not read the Cursor parsing code to confirm that a negative offset in a client-supplied cursor string is accepted. I am also assuming the queryset is a plain Django QuerySet.
